sammendrag: This thesis investigates how unemployment insurance (UI) affects individuals during and after unemployment. Drawing on historical evidence from recent recessions in the United States, publicly available data, behavioral insights, and mathematical modeling, it argues that the benefits of extending UI outweigh the potential costs. The analysis incorporates a wide range of sources, including empirical economic studies using regression models and psychology and business research that highlight behavioral responses to financial stress and job insecurity. By combining quantitative data with behavioral context, the thesis offers a more comprehensive understanding of how extended UI influences job search decisions, wage outcomes, and overall labor market efficiency. It also addresses common misconceptions surrounding UI, particularly the belief that more generous benefits discourage work, by incorporating theoretical models such as the labor-discipline framework. In doing so, the thesis presents a persuasive case for why UI should be seen not only as a safety net but also as a mechanism for improving employment quality and economic resilience. Through this interdisciplinary approach, it contributes to ongoing debates about the role of social welfare policy in shaping modern labor markets.
tittel: Benefits of Extended Unemployment Insurance on Post-Unemployment Outcomes
